name: inprocess-obi-apb-three-ip-timer-i2c-spi-f1f6
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU reaches three independent APB3 MMIO targets by address in one session: the PULP timer (the one F5 target), the PULP I2C held at idle pins, and the PULP SPI with its serial inputs pinned. The declaration is a targets list, so the entry builds one generated model per row and routes every case by address; no CPU x IP branch exists.
notes: Three APB3 target rows, one generated model each. Windows: timer 0x40001000..0x40001fff, I2C 0x40002000..0x40002fff, SPI 0x20002000..0x20002fff. All are the profiles' own 4 KiB windows, 4 KiB aligned, pairwise disjoint, and disjoint from the RAM image 0x10000..0x30000.

Only the timer declares the four F5 facts (configs/behaviors/pulp_timer_f5.json), so it is the one target that owns the CPU's single external IRQ line. The I2C declares interrupts: [] and the SPI declares none; both are still reachable by address for F2/F4, which is exactly what makes this a three-IP routing session and not three IRQ sources.

The I2C pad inputs scl_pad_i/sda_pad_i and the SPI serial inputs sdi0..sdi3 are held at their idle values in both fixed_inputs and tuning.fixed_inputs: the target request builder reads tuning and the generated header reads fixed_inputs, so the two declarations have to agree. No 32-bit pad group is selected, so the one-pad-model rule does not apply.

No dma_profile is declared, so F6 is refused by name (unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:apb3) rather than served from an absent model; the three targets and the six target-routed records are the whole session.
